usids.rsrp_spatial_pattern: Compact deep-blue cluster (all pixels > -80 dBm excellent) centered at tower ~33.023N, -96.703W. Yellow dominance boundary encloses a small, roughly circular area of 26 pixels. Signal remains uniformly excellent throughout the interior; no degradation gradient within the boundary. Backup-mode pixels extend N and NE of the boundary in teal/green tones (~-70 to -78 dBm) — still good quality but below dominance threshold.

Tower positioned NW of USID_00 (~33.027, -96.707). Deep-blue signal (excellent) dominates the NW and center of USID_00's area as shown by heavy overlap with the red-dashed USID_00 boundary. Coverage fades toward the SE corner of USID_00's area to teal/green (~-70 dBm). Own dominance boundary (yellow) is offset NW from USID_00's boundary — USID_27 is the strongest backup in the NW quadrant of USID_00's zone.

Tower positioned ESE of USID_00 (~33.022, -96.699). Deep-blue excellent signal covers the central and SE portion of USID_00's area (red-dashed boundary). USID_29's own dominance (yellow) sits to the SE of USID_00. Signal weakens at the NW edge of USID_00's boundary. Good backup coverage for the E/SE half of USID_00's area.

Tower located S of USID_00 (~33.020, -96.706). Coverage of USID_00's area (red-dashed) is limited to the southern edge — only the bottom strip of USID_00's boundary sees USID_41 signal. One bright-green pixel visible at the NE edge of the overlap, but most backup in the south. The NW quadrant of USID_00's area receives very little USID_41 signal.

Tower positioned SE of USID_00 (~33.021, -96.700). Provides deep-blue excellent signal in the SE quadrant of USID_00's area (red-dashed boundary). Own yellow dominance boundary is south of USID_00's zone. Lighter green signal (good, ~-80 dBm) visible at the NW fringes of the overlap area. Complements USID_29 coverage in the eastern half of USID_00.

Tower located S/SSW of USID_00 (~33.019, -96.703). Coverage of USID_00's area is marginal — only 2 pixels at the extreme southern tip of USID_00's boundary fall within USID_31's reach. Own yellow dominance boundary is well south of USID_00's zone. Deep-blue signal in its own area but the overlap with USID_00 is minimal.

target_load_analysis.coverage_hole_assessment: 3 pixels (11.54% of USID_00's 26 dominant pixels) have no backup coverage. This is above the 5% minor threshold but below 20%. Located at the S/SW boundary edge where neither USID_27 (NW tower) nor USID_29/37 (SE towers) reach. Users in this fringe strip will have no handover target upon shutdown.

per_backup.assessment: USID_27 is the primary backup, absorbing 61.5% of USID_00's dominant pixels with excellent in-zone RSRP of -57.6 dBm (100% above good threshold). Post-outage load factor of 0.013 is negligible, confirming no capacity stress; the SINR regime is mixed (intermediate impact, neither fully noise- nor interference-limited).

USID_29 covers 42.3% of USID_00's area with good in-zone RSRP (-58.83 dBm, 100% above good). The mostly_mild SINR regime indicates that backups are already competitive in this zone, reducing post-shutdown degradation. Post-outage load factor 0.011 presents no capacity concern.

USID_41 absorbs 34.6% of USID_00's dominant pixels with strong in-zone RSRP of -58.5 dBm (100% above good). Despite being a 4G-heavy site (8×4G, 2×5G), its in-zone signal quality is excellent; post-outage load factor 0.012 is well below any risk threshold.

USID_37 covers 26.9% of USID_00's area (SE quadrant) with good RSRP of -58.71 dBm and the lowest post-outage load factor (0.005) of all backups. It provides solid SE-quadrant redundancy complementing USID_29 with negligible load impact.

USID_31 is a marginal backup, absorbing only 7.7% of USID_00's area (2 pixels at the southern tip). In-zone RSRP is -57.54 dBm (good), and post-outage load factor 0.008 is trivial. Its contribution is minimal but clean where it does overlap.

verdict_reasoning: All five backup USIDs show post_outage_load_factor <= 0.013, far below the 0.50 medium-risk threshold, confirming no capacity overload on any backup site.
100% of covered pixels (88.46% of USID_00's area) achieve rsrp_pct_above_good_in_zone = 100.0% for every backup, indicating excellent handover signal quality throughout the covered portion.

Coverage hole fraction is 11.54% (3 pixels), which is a moderate gap but does not affect the load redistribution verdict since the remaining 88.46% transitions cleanly with no overload; coverage holes are a coverage gap issue, not a load overload issue.

key_findings_for_stage3: Coverage holes (11.54%, 3 pixels) are concentrated at the S/SW edge of USID_00's dominance boundary — where neither USID_27 (NW) nor USID_29/37 (SE) footprints reach.
USID_27 provides the dominant backup signal across the NW and center of USID_00's area, with strong blue RSRP visible throughout the NW quadrant of the boundary.
USID_29 and USID_37 together cover the E/SE portion of USID_00's area, providing a complementary eastern backup corridor.

The SINR map shows predominantly cool blue/cyan tones inside USID_00's dominant area, consistent with target_dom_low_sinr_fraction=0.6923 — interference-limited regime means backup signals were already competitive before the outage.

reasons: All statistics sourced directly from preprocessing with no derived or estimated values.
Image spatial claims are consistent with per_backup absorption fractions — USID_27 dominates NW (highest absorption 0.6154), USID_29/37 cover SE (second/third highest).
